work.text: A hosted computer-vision model. The miner trains a model for one or more Elements (named tasks such as detecting players in football footage), deploys it on Chutes, a separate Bittensor subnet that rents model hosting, and records its fingerprint on chain. What is paid for is the model's answers to validator challenges, frame by frame, under a latency gate.
work.quote: raw footage becomes structured, decision-ready data in real time, with early deployments focused on professional sports

scoring.text: Per Element, each answer is scored on pillars (for example overlap with the answer key, player count, smoothness, role), each pillar times its manifest weight, summed. The sum is gated: subtract the Element's baseline theta, floor at delta_floor, multiply by beta, a difficulty factor. The answer key is real ground truth or a SAM3 segmentation. The winner is the highest average over at least 30 challenges in a 3-day window.

split.text: Winner takes all, per Element. Each Element carries a weight in the signed manifest, and the whole of that weight goes to the Element's single winner on the open-source track. On the private track the top three split the Element weight 0.80, 0.15, 0.05. Weight left unassigned, for an Element with no winner, goes to a fallback UID, 6 by default.
split.quote: PRIVATE_TRACK_RANKED_WEIGHT_SHARES = (0.80, 0.15, 0.05); share = float(elem_weight); weights_by_uid[winner_uid] = weights_by_uid.get(winner_uid, 0.0) + share

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot. Commit-reveal is off. The code names one central validator whose scoring shards pick the winners; audit validators spot-check miners rather than score them. A validator that finds no central registry on chain falls back to its own local scores. Weights go through a separate signer service.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled False, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9
judges.disagrees: The draft whitepaper (notes/toward-manako/wp.md) describes an aggregation service merging every validator's shards with stake-weighted MAD outlier pruning; the code at the pinned commit reads winners from a single SCOREVISION_CENTRAL_VALIDATOR_HOTKEY and falls back to local data when it is absent.

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The validator's weights loop runs every 150 blocks, 30 minutes, by default; the runner scores each Element every 300 blocks unless the manifest sets its own window. Winners are chosen over a rolling 3-day window with a 30-challenge minimum. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 7,500 blocks, about 25 hours.

buyer.text: Nobody is named. The front page describes a research company building models and offers a Console link and a Let's Talk contact form. There is no price, no product page, no endpoint and no customer named in text on the site or in the repository; the README says early deployments focus on professional sports. The miner's income is emission.
buyer.quote: We're building models that turn raw video into structured intelligence.

exploits.text: Copying a rival's model: when two miners score alike on the same challenges, recent and historical samples are compared, and a confirmed copy loses the tie to the earlier on-chain commit block. Slow but accurate models are zeroed by the latency gate. A blacklist file in the repository holds 120 hotkeys, reason unstated, and any weight to them is removed before signing.
exploits.quote: if hk and hk in blacklisted_hotkeys: weights_by_uid.pop(uid, None)
